content: 1. UNAIDS data was accessed on March 12, 2020. 2. The Pan American Health Organization published a report titled Tuberculosis in the Americas, 2018, in Washington, D.C., in 2018. This report was accessed on March 12, 2020. 3. The World Health Organization (WHO) released guidelines in 2017 for managing advanced HIV disease and the rapid initiation of antiretroviral therapy. These guidelines were accessed on March 12, 2020. 4. Adenis AA and colleagues conducted a modeling study comparing the burden of HIV-associated histoplasmosis with tuberculosis in Latin America, published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases in 2018. 5. Calderon EJ and colleagues discussed Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia as a public health problem in Latin America in Expert Review of Anti-Infective Therapy in 2013. 6. Rajasingham R and colleagues updated the global burden of HIV-associated cryptococcal meningitis in The Lancet Infectious Diseases in 2017. 7. The Neglected Histoplasmosis in Latin America Group highlighted disseminated histoplasmosis as a critical and overlooked health issue in Central and South America in AIDS in 2016. 8. Bahr NC and colleagues reviewed histoplasmosis infections worldwide, emphasizing the need to consider regions beyond the Ohio River Valley, in Current Tropical Medicine Reports in 2015. 9. Adenis A and colleagues conducted a comparative study on tuberculosis and histoplasmosis among HIV-infected patients, published in The American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 2014. 10. Hage CA and colleagues provided an evidence-based approach to diagnosing and managing histoplasmosis in Seminars in Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine in 2015. 11. Pasqualotto AC and Queiroz-Telles F discussed how histoplasmosis has surpassed tuberculosis in importance in Latin America in The Lancet Infectious Diseases in 2018. 12. Caceres DH and Valdes A examined the co-occurrence of histoplasmosis and tuberculosis in individuals with advanced HIV in Journal of Fungi (Basel) in 2019. 13. WHO published guidelines in 2018 for diagnosing, preventing, and managing cryptococcal disease in HIV-infected adults, adolescents, and children. These were accessed on March 12, 2020. 14. WHO released its second model list of essential in vitro diagnostics in 2019, which was accessed on March 12, 2020. 15. WHO also published its model list of essential medicines in 2019, accessed on March 12, 2020. 16. Azar MM and Hage CA provided clinical perspectives on diagnosing and managing histoplasmosis in Clinics in Chest Medicine in 2017. 17. Samayoa B and colleagues reported high mortality and co-infection rates in a prospective cohort of HIV/AIDS patients with histoplasmosis in Guatemala in The American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 2017. 18. Caceres DH and colleagues demonstrated that implementing a training course increased histoplasmosis diagnoses in Colombia, as published in The American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 2015. 19. Caceres DH and colleagues conducted a meta-analysis on the diagnostic performance of assays for progressive disseminated histoplasmosis in advanced HIV, published in Journal of Fungi (Basel) in 2019. 20. De Pauw B and colleagues revised definitions of invasive fungal disease for the European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer and the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases Mycoses Study Group in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2008. 21. Bansal N and colleagues explored the utility of urinary histoplasma antigen testing in tuberculosis-endemic regions in Mycoses in 2019. 22. Falci DR and colleagues conducted a multicenter prospective cohort study in Brazil, highlighting the underdiagnosis of histoplasmosis in people living with HIV/AIDS, published in Open Forum Infectious Diseases in 2019. 23. Wheat LJ and colleagues reviewed clinical findings, diagnosis, and treatment of disseminated histoplasmosis in AIDS patients in Medicine (Baltimore) in 1990. 24. Johnson PC and colleagues compared the safety and efficacy of liposomal amphotericin B with conventional amphotericin B for histoplasmosis induction therapy in AIDS patients in Annals of Internal Medicine in 2002. 25. Wheat LJ and colleagues updated clinical practice guidelines for managing histoplasmosis in 2007, published by the Infectious Diseases Society of America in Clinical Infectious Diseases. 26. Murphy RA and colleagues discussed challenges in managing disseminated progressive histoplasmosis in HIV-infected patients in resource-limited settings in Open Forum Infectious Diseases in 2015. 27. Damasceno LS and colleagues identified determinants of relapse and mortality in HIV-infected patients with disseminated histoplasmosis in northeastern Brazil in Mycoses in 2014. 28. Myint T and colleagues conducted a multicenter study on outcomes and relapse factors in HIV/AIDS patients with histoplasmosis, published in Medicine (Baltimore) in 2014. 29. Murray M and Hine P reviewed treatments for progressive disseminated histoplasmosis in people living with HIV in Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2020. 30. Wheat J and colleagues evaluated fluconazole treatment for histoplasmosis in AIDS patients in a study by the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases AIDS Clinical Trials Group, published in The American Journal of Medicine in 1997. 31. Wheat J and colleagues assessed itraconazole treatment for disseminated histoplasmosis in AIDS patients in The American Journal of Medicine in 1995. 32. Drew RH reviewed pharmacotherapy for disseminated histoplasmosis in AIDS patients in Annals of Pharmacotherapy in 1993. 33. Norris S and colleagues studied fluconazole's role in preventing histoplasmosis relapse in AIDS patients in The American Journal of Medicine in 1994. 34. Sharkey-Mathis PK and colleagues compared itraconazole and fluconazole for treating histoplasmosis in AIDS patients in Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 1993. 35. Hecht FM and colleagues conducted a multicenter trial on itraconazole maintenance therapy for histoplasmosis in AIDS patients in Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes and Human Retrovirology in 1997. 36. WHO updated recommendations on firstand second-line antiretroviral regimens in 2019, accessed on March 12, 2020. 37. Negroni R and colleagues evaluated antifungal treatment and secondary prophylaxis for AIDS-related histoplasmosis in Revista Iberoamericana de Micología in 2017. 38. Melzani A and colleagues reviewed immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome associated with Histoplasma capsulatum in HIV patients over 20 years in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2020. 39. Zolopa A and colleagues demonstrated that early antiretroviral therapy reduces AIDS progression and death in individuals with acute opportunistic infections in PLoS One in 2009. 40. Drayton J and colleagues reported that co-administration of rifampin and itraconazole results in undetectable serum itraconazole levels in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 1994. 41. Agudelo CA and colleagues studied tuberculosis and histoplasmosis co-infection in AIDS patients in The American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 2012. 42. Andes D and colleagues reviewed antifungal drug monitoring for established and emerging indications in Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy in 2009. 43. Bellmann R and Smuszkiewicz P discussed the pharmacokinetics of antifungal drugs and their implications for optimized treatment in Infection in 2017. 44. Bahr NC and colleagues showed that standardized electrolyte supplementation and fluid management improve survival during amphotericin therapy for cryptococcal meningitis in resource-limited settings in Open Forum Infectious Diseases in 2014. 45. Dismukes WE and colleagues evaluated itraconazole therapy for blastomycosis and histoplasmosis in The American Journal of Medicine in 1992. 46. Lestner JM and colleagues examined the toxicodynamics of itraconazole and its implications for therapeutic drug monitoring in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2009. 47. Caceres DH and colleagues highlighted the role of co-infections in AIDS patients with progressive disseminated histoplasmosis in Medical Mycology Case Reports in 2018. 48. Caceres DH and colleagues validated an ELISA for detecting Histoplasma capsulatum antigenuria in Colombian AIDS patients for diagnosis and therapy follow-up in Clinical Vaccine Immunology in 2014. 49. Caceres DH and colleagues evaluated a lateral flow assay for rapid diagnosis of progressive disseminated histoplasmosis in Colombian AIDS patients in Mycoses in 2020. 50. WHO published guidelines for declaring interests for experts in 2017, accessed on March 12, 2020. 51. WHO released a handbook for guideline development in 2018, accessed on March 12, 2020. 52. Moher D and colleagues introduced the PRISMA statement for systematic reviews and meta-analyses in Journal of Clinical Epidemiology in 2009. 53. Guyatt GH and colleagues presented the GRADE framework for rating evidence quality and recommendation strength in BMJ in 2008. 54. Caceres DH and colleagues reported on the current situation of histoplasmosis in the Americas in the Manaus Declaration, published in Current Fungal Infection Reports in 2019.
